title: Hourglass burn smoothing & price levers — Q4 contingency proforma
body:
Executive summary:

This sheet proposes an operational playbook to smooth hourly/monthly burn over Q4 using a combination of targeted headcount phasing, a short-term microburst reserve, and a tiered price-levers experiment for new customers. The goal is to preserve runway while keeping enough runway for go-to-market seasonality and Dedicated onboarding commitments.

Key ideas: compact hiring windows + temporary contractor overlay; a small paid-reserve product ("microburst") to capture customers who will pay premium for guaranteed burst capacity during spikes; a 4-week price-lever experiment (three arms) to understand elasticity at the mid-market and AI-native startup segments.

High-level results we want from the model:
- Keep monthly burn within +/- 6% of plan under moderate demand swings (+/- 25% token volume).
- Delay full-time hiring by 6–8 weeks (where feasible) while preserving throughput via contractor bursts and on-call overtime for critical SRE/infra roles.
- Identify price points that offset ~20–35% of incremental GPU cost during spikes.

Assumptions (base case):
- Current committed slabs: 60% slab/40% on-demand mix for hosted API revenue.
- Average blended token margin (pre-provisioning cost): 28% at current price bands.
- Q4 expected token volume growth: +18% baseline, with 1-in-5 spike weeks reaching +60% (sales campaigns).
- Hiring lead time: 8–10 weeks for L4-L5 engineers, 4–6 weeks for contractors.
- Microburst product revenue capture rate: conservative 10% of customers offered opt-in in first month.

Scenario sensitivity snapshot (excerpt):
(Columns = Scenario | Token vol delta | Price delta | HC freeze | Net burn delta vs plan)
scenario_table: HC freeze | +18% | 0% | full hiring freeze | -4.1% (saves hires but increases overtime)
headcount_plan:
Hiring phasing and overlays:
- Week 0–4: pause non-critical external hiring that is not customer-facing; prioritize product ops and infra critical hires (SRE lead) only.
- Week 4–10: staggered offers for L4 engineers with start dates week 10–14.
- Contractor overlay: budget for 8 FTE-weeks equivalent contractors for infra and model ops to cover peak onboarding windows.
- On-call overtime: temporary bump in contractor/on-call stipend capped at 6 weeks during peak.
- Internal redeploy: identify 2 PM/engineering pairs who can be rotated for Dedicated onboarding weeks to reduce external hires.

Estimated headcount P&L impact (quick numbers):
- Delaying 3 hires by 8 weeks = ~ $240k GTY cash deferral (smoothing effect).
- Contractor overlay (8 FTE-weeks) = ~$48k incremental cash in Q4.
- Overtime/stipend = ~$18k cap.
- Net Q4 cash saving (headcount deferral - overlay/stipend) ~= $174k.
pricing_experiment:
Three-arm price experiment (4 weeks):
- Arm A (control): current price bands.
- Arm B (tiered microburst add-on): +12% effective price for customers who opt into burst SLAs (2-hour guaranteed response, billed per-minute token premium).
- Arm C (temporary discount to stimulate volume): -8% introductory discount for selected cold-start segments to measure volume elasticity.

KPIs to measure: opt-in rate to microburst, delta in token volume per customer, churn signal within 30 days, incremental GPU cost coverage percentage.

Runbook triggers:
- If opt-in rate > 18% and incremental margin covers > 25% GPU spike, scale microburst to 20% of new signups.
- If Arm C shows >25% new volume but margin < 10%, cap discount regionally and shift to Arm B.

Open questions / risks:
- Customer backlash risk if pricing experiments leak; need segmented rollout and legal pre-clear.
- Operational risk: microburst requires routing changes, quota enforcement and SLA automation in Console—requires 2-week infra sprint.
- Churn risk from Arm C discounting cannibalizing slab sales in existing customers.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Finance: finalize P&L simulation inputs and add fine-grain token mix by customer cohort (Diego) — 1 week.
- Product & Console: spec microburst SLA, quota, and billing events (Priya) — 10 business days.
- Solutions engineering: identify 3 pilot customers for microburst (Ethan) — 2 weeks.
- Legal: review T&Cs for add-on premium product (Ava) — 5 business days.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally tactical and iterative: model is conservative on opt-in and elasticity.
- Attachments: quick simulation csv (linked in artifacts) with the full burn smoothing matrices by cohort.

Quick links: Confluence playbook above, JIRA-FIN-1412 (pricing experiment ticket), GH PR for simulation code.
conclusions: Recommendation: run the 4-week three-arm pricing experiment in parallel with a hiring pause on non-critical roles and fund an 8 FTE-week contractor overlay. If microburst opt-in and margin metrics meet thresholds, launch as paid add-on and use proceeds to subsidize contractor cost during next quarter. Follow up with detailed per-customer cohort simulation runbook (FIN to hand off to Product/SE).
notes:
Informal notes / brainstorming fragments:
- Could we pair microburst with reserved capacity credits? sells comfort to mid-market.
- Should we pre-authorize a $200k contingency pool to be deployed automatically if token volumes exceed 1.5x for two consecutive weeks?
- Consider short-term placement of senior infra hire on a 4-month contract-to-hire to lower lead time risk.

Slack refs and internal signals: thread #finance-updates 2026-10-25 (opt-in pricing idea), #product-console spike-automation-requests (Oct 2026).
